decisions.reason: The client explicitly says the PIR and touch pull-downs are correct and need no change; their independently stated biasing configuration is already represented.

Changing the button bias resistors does not alter the connector inventory, GPIO assignments, control placement, or existing connector roles; pin 1 remaining GND confirms continuity rather than a connector-state change.
The source changes resistor biasing and button polarity without reassigning any ESP32 GPIO.
R16, R17, and R18 concern panel button and switch inputs, not the BOOT or reset controls and their timing capacitors.
The input-biasing decision does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module, part number, or pin count.
The source does not change breakout coverage, placement, connector style, or header pitch.
The shared references to 3.3V, GND, and pull resistors are incidental; the source does not address the e-paper backlight circuit.
The button pull-up decision does not change addressable-LED power, data GPIO, level shifting, or standby control.
Using the existing 3.3V rail for button pull-ups does not change the rail voltage, DCDC1 programming, rating, or compensation behavior.
The source concerns local panel-input circuitry and does not alter any interboard connector, pinout, or board power-chain requirement.
The button-biasing change does not alter the AXP2101 battery path, system rails, charging behavior, or efficiency requirement.
The source does not change the standalone USB regulator, activation condition, powered load coverage, or unresolved regulator-current question.
